ruling.recommended_action: Decline the refund request: inform the rider that the $6.61 cancellation fee was validly imposed under NS-1 (driver confirmed arrival in range at 18:24:35 and waited 3 min 50 s before cancelling), that Ryde has no weather or grace-period exception to the 3-minute no-show threshold, and that no account action attaches to this trip.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a driver-cancelled no-show fee case, so NS-0 routes it to NS-1: the fee stands only if (i) arrival was confirmed, (ii) the driver was within 200 m of the pickup at that moment, and (iii) he then stayed at the pickup continuously for more than 3 minutes until cancelling [F4][NS-0][NS-1]. The trace settles all three elements as ✓ and none of them is left for me to interpret; the only open item flagged is the SAFE-1 screen.

On (i) and (ii): the arrival confirmation is a driver tap, and at that tap (18:24:35) the driver was 41 m from the pickup point, inside the arrival radius, with the closest approach overall 38 m [F6][F1]. Both sides concede these elements in their rebuttals [F6][NS-1].

On (iii): the system record measures 230 seconds (3 min 50 s) continuously inside the radius after the 18:24:35 tap, against the default threshold of more than 180 s, and the driver remained stationary at 41 m from 18:24:15 all the way to the 18:28:25 cancellation [F6][F3][F4][NS-1]. NS-1 expressly disregards time spent near the pickup before the tap, so I clock the wait from 18:24:35 as the rider advocate correctly argues; even on that stricter clock the post-tap wait exceeds the threshold by 50 seconds, so condition (iii) is satisfied [F6][F3][NS-1]. The driver's post-trip statement claiming "more than 4 minutes" is a statement, but it does not matter: the fee is supported by the timeline record itself, not by his assertion [F13][F6][NS-1].

The rider's strongest point is her 18:25 message asking for two more minutes [F10][F9]; the driver cancelled at 18:28:25, i.e. roughly 1 min 25 s after her requested extension expired, but NS-1 contains no grace period beyond the 3-minute continuous wait, and the heavy rain recorded at 18.5 mm is not a weather exception to that condition [F10][F16][F4][NS-1]. The rider advocate's own admission that NS-1(iii) is met on the plain reading of the rule therefore carries the case [F6][NS-1].

Because every NS-1 element is met, the $6.61 fee recorded in F7 and F4 was validly imposed and no refund sum arises; NS-7 timeliness is uncontested [F7][F4][NS-7]. The rider advocate's request for an account flag under RD-6 fails at its own precondition: RD-6 requires that the case be established against the driver, i.e. a refund greater than 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach, and here the answer is no_action [F4][F6][RD-6]. The driver's profile history (2 upheld no-show disputes) is a profile fact and cannot decide or add to this trip's outcome [F18][RD-6]. Confidence is high because the policy elements track settled trace items, with the only judicial reading being whether the rider's extension request suspends the wait condition, which the policy text does not allow [F10][NS-1].

Correct as a statement of the rule but inapplicable to this record: every NS-1 element (i)(ii)(iii) is met, so NS-2's refund of the $6.61 is not triggered [F6][F3][F7][NS-1].

Accepted that the timestamped chat record carries more weight than the driver's statement, but it does not help the rider: F13 is not needed to support the fee, which rests on the timeline and GPS facts alone [F13][F6][F3][NS-1].

The rider's clean profile (865-day account, 4.5 rating, no upheld disputes) is a profile fact that cannot alone decide the case; NS-1 turns on the driver's arrival, position and waiting time, all of which are met [F17][F6][F3][NS-1].

RD-6 requires the case to be established against the driver (a refund greater than 0 or a recorded RD-1 breach) before a flag_account attaches; here the fee was validly imposed and the outcome is no_action, so the driver's 2 upheld no-show disputes support no account action [F18][F4][F6][RD-6].

The heavy rain (18.5 mm, thundery showers) is accepted as fact and explains the rider's request, but NS-1 contains no weather exception to the continuous-wait condition, and the recorded wait exceeded 3 minutes [F16][F10][F6][NS-1].

The claim that a $6.61 voucher must issue under NS-7 fails because no refund sum arises: the charged item was validly imposed under NS-1, so NS-7's voucher mechanism has nothing to apply to [F7][F4][NS-7][NS-1].
Withdrawn by the driver advocate and in any event correct that no dishonesty attaches: the tap was inside the arrival radius, so no abuse-of-button flag arises [F6][NS-2].
